newsitem.title: THAILAND: Deng death impact seen limited in sugar market.
newsitem.headline: Deng death impact seen limited in sugar market.

text.p: The Thai sugar market shrugged off the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, saying it was unlikely to affect sugar and other commodities markets, at least over the short-term, trade sources said.
"It has been long rumoured and not a sudden death. After all he is 92," said Hu Feng Nian, a manager at Kerry Foodstuffs.
"The impact seemed limited to stock markets only. I don't think it will influence the sugar and other commodities markets even though it is big news," he said.
Traders and industry sources said they did not expect the death of Deng to immediately bring about political and economic changes.

"When analysing if Deng's death will affect the market in term of demand, supplies or policy, one has to see if his death will change political or economic courses. And my opinion is it will not," said Surat Abhikelophan, head of marketing at Thai Cane and Sugar Corp.
"Or if there's any changes that might be caused by a post-Deng power struggle, I don't think it will be substantial enough to affect the big economic picture," he added.
Deng's death barely moved premiums in the raw sugar market which were quoted around $0.20/0.30 cents a lb over New York futures for March/May deliveries, hardly changed from earlier this week.
